class.name: CgameFoveatedShading
class.brief_description: Builds and applies Variable Rate Shading density maps for a centered subject.
class.description: [CgameFoveatedShading] implements foveated rendering for games whose camera keeps the player near the screen center (top-down and third-person views). It builds an elliptical shading-rate map: full rate in the middle, a 2x2 ring around it and 4x4 shading in the corners, then assigns it to a [Viewport] using [constant Viewport.VRS_TEXTURE]. Quality levels [code]0[/code] (Performance) and [code]1[/code] (Balanced) enable foveation on the [code]forward_plus[/code] and [code]mobile[/code] renderers. Levels [code]2[/code] and [code]3[/code], and the [code]gl_compatibility[/code] renderer, always shade at full rate. GPUs without VRS support ignore the texture. The rate map uses the Godot VRS density encoding: red is the horizontal and green the vertical rate, where [code]0[/code] is 1x, [code]85[/code] is 2x and [code]170[/code] is 4x. The generated texture is cached and reused while the viewport size and profile stay the same.

method.name: apply
method.description: Applies the profile for [param level] and [param rendering_method] to [param viewport]. Returns [code]true[/code] when VRS was enabled. When the profile is disabled, VRS is turned off, the texture is cleared and [code]false[/code] is returned. The map is sized in 16 pixel tiles of the viewport's visible rectangle.

method.name: build_map
method.description: Builds an [constant Image.FORMAT_RGB8] rate map of [param size] texels (clamped to at least 1x1). [param inner] and [param outer] are radii in normalized screen space where [code]1.0[/code] reaches the middle of an edge. Inside [param inner] the rate is 1x1; between the radii it is 2x2 near the top and bottom and 2x1 near the sides; outside [param outer] it is 4x4.

method.name: settings
method.description: Returns the profile for a quality level as a dictionary with [code]enabled[/code] and, when enabled, [code]inner[/code] and [code]outer[/code] radii.
